subject: Nimble POC — model shortlist & proposed pilot plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wu <emma.wu@nimblefin.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nimblefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Nimble POC — model shortlist & proposed pilot plan

Hi Emma / Liam,

Thanks again for the demo time today — useful to see the 3 core flows you care about (statement extraction, customer intent classification, and follow-on summarization). As promised, quick recap of the model candidates we recommend for a 2-week pilot plus the rationale and next steps: 

Shortlist (recommended for pilot)
- Falcon-RS-7B (balanced): Strong baseline on extraction tests, median latency ~45ms/token on A100 reserved pool. Best cost/quality balance for initial live traffic.
- Redwood-2.7b-quant (latency/cost optimized): Quantized variant with very low cost and P50 latency ~28ms/token; good for high-throughput classification but lower headroom on long-form summarization quality.
- LlamaX-13B-optim (quality-first): Best on abstractive summarization and hallucination resistance in our small eval sets; higher token-cost and P95 latency (~180ms/token) but useful as a fallback for edge cases.

Why these three: they give you a cascade/fallback strategy (fast cheap -> balanced -> quality). That maps to the SLAs you described: 100ms target for interactive classification, and higher tolerance for batch summarization.

Benchmarks & artifacts attached: nimble_benchmarks_20280118.csv (throughput/latency/cost by model), nimble_prompt_pack_v2.zip (call/edge-case prompts we used), model_eval_notebook.ipynb (notebook to reproduce the tests). Full Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bNimbleBenchmarks

Pilot proposal (2 weeks):
- Inclusion: all three models behind Redwood routing (policy = latency-first, with fallback)
- Metrics: per-route token cost, p50/p95 latency, hallucination rate on curated test set, and quality regression alerts (we'll run nightly evals).
- Deliverables: shared eval notebook, demo dashboard, regression alert thresholds, and a short playbook for failover.
- Cost: rough estimates below (per 100k tokens) — final numbers depend on committed capacity.

Estimated cost (per 100k tokens, rough)
- Falcon-RS-7B: $28
- Redwood-2.7b-quant: $9
- LlamaX-13B-optim: $72

Next steps
1) If you’re comfortable, we’ll provision a 2-week Dedicated trial environment and seed it with your prompt pack.
2) We’ll run a 48-hour sanity sweep using your high-risk prompt subset, then open the pilot to limited traffic.
3) Kickoff call (30m) to lock on goals and measurement hygiene.

If you want a narrower starter (2-model) option, recommend Falcon-RS-7B + Redwood-2.7b-quant for speed-to-value.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate availability for the kickoff.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--- Attachments: nimble_benchmarks_20280118.csv (CSV, 120KB), nimble_prompt_pack_v2.zip (ZIP, 4 files), model_eval_notebook.ipynb (Notebook)
From: Emma Wu <emma.wu@nimblefin.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nimblefin.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2028 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimble POC — model shortlist & proposed pilot plan

Jordan — great summary, thanks. A couple quick clarifying items from our side before we lock the pilot: 

1) Hallucination / fact-safety: We saw some hallucination in the demo for long-form summaries. Can you quantify the expected hallucination rate for the three models on our test prompts? We need a baseline number to include in the evaluation criteria.

2) Cost math: The per-100k estimates are helpful — can you break down the cost by token consumption per flow (we have short classification calls (~20 tokens per call) and long summaries (~1.2k tokens))?

3) Compliance question: We run financial data with PII. Can the Dedicated trial be configured to route through our VPC and use our KMS? Also need to pull SOC 2 evidence for the security questionnaire before we send this to procurement.

4) SLA ask: For interactive classification we want to keep tail latency under 120ms. Is that realistic with the Falcon-RS-7B route under pilot traffic?

If these look good, we’re ready to proceed with the 2-week pilot. Liam and I are available for a kickoff Tue 1/31 afternoon PST.

—Emma
VP Product, Nimble Financials
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wu <emma.wu@nimblefin.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nimblefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jan 2028 11:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimble POC — model shortlist & proposed pilot plan

Emma — great questions, answered inline below. I also attached an "eval-run-template.csv" you can use to map cost/flow.

1) Hallucination numbers
- On Nimble's long-summary test slice (n=250 curated cases): LlamaX-13B-optim ~3.6% hallucination (highest quality on the set), Falcon-RS-7B ~7.9%, Redwood-2.7b-quant ~12.4%. These are our measured end-to-end hallucination flags using your rubric (missing fact, invented entity, contradictory output). We’ll include nightly regression alerts if anything moves >1.5% from baseline.

2) Cost by flow (approx)
- Classification (~20 tokens): 
  - Falcon-RS-7B: $0.006 per call
  - Redwood-2.7b-quant: $0.002 per call
  - LlamaX-13B-optim: $0.015 per call
- Long summary (~1.2k tokens):
  - Falcon-RS-7B: $0.34 per summary
  - Redwood-2.7b-quant: $0.11 per summary (but quality caveat)
  - LlamaX-13B-optim: $1.18 per summary

3) Compliance / Dedicated trial 
- Yes, we can provision the Dedicated trial behind your VPC and plug in your KMS for key wrapping. SOC 2 evidence (summary report + control matrix) is available — I’ll send the redacted PDF to your procurement contact after we confirm NDAs.

4) SLA & tail latency
- Under the pilot capacity we intend to reserve, Falcon-RS-7B has historically held p95 <120ms for interactive payloads at the scale you quoted (peak concurrency ~70). We’ll set up continuous tail-latency tracing in Redwood Console and can auto-escalate to the LlamaX route for suspect requests.

Pilot operational notes
- Routing policy: latency-first, but with a fallback to LlamaX for flagged summaries or when hallucination risk score >0.6.
- Regression guardrails: nightly evals, daily synthetic checks, and an on-call escalation to the Redwood SRE on any quality regression.

If you approve, next step: I’ll open a HubSpot pilot record and route to provisioning. Also attaching eval-run-template.csv to help you map the expected monthly cost if productionized.

—Jordan

--- Attachment: eval-run-template.csv (CSV, 4KB)

Can you prepare a 2-slide cost/ROI summary showing (a) expected monthly token spend ranges, (b) risk windows for hallucinations, and (c) recommended rollout cadence (canary -> 50% -> 100%)?

If we can get that into Emma by Tue 1/24, I think procurement will move faster. I can handle the commercial terms once Emma confirms the PO path.
